```plato
//==
// # Core
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Core comparison
//  - Core logic

library Core
{
    //==
    // # Core comparison
    //
    // Derived functionality for the comparison interfaces
    // (`core.concepts.plato`): the strict/relaxed relational operators,
    // extrema, range tests, and three-way comparison, all built on the single
    // `LessThanOrEquals` primitive of `IOrderable`
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_order).
    //
    // This file also carries the shared provenance note for the whole
    // Derived functionality for the `core.concepts.plato` and
    // `algebra.concepts.plato` interfaces.
    // Every function's first parameter is interface-typed, so the function becomes
    // available on every type implementing that interface. Bodies are pure
    // expressions built only from members declared on the interface, its inherited
    // interfaces, or other functions in this library.

    //==
    // IOrderable
    //
    // LessThanOrEquals itself cannot be derived here: it IS the primitive of
    // IOrderable, so there is nothing on the interface surface to build it from.
    // The only mechanical lever for the outstanding LessThanOrEquals obligations
    // is a *narrower* interface whose implementors share a carrier with a known
    // order — that is `IIndex` (single `Value: Integer`), and its generic body
    // lives in `collections.library.plato` because P2 owns `IIndex`
    // (LIBRARIES.md rule 10). It discharges every typed-index implementor.
    //
    // The remaining implementors have no shared derivable order and each needs a
    // concrete body in its owning package, not a generic one here:
    //   - Rational (numbers) — ordering is a/b <= c/d via cross-multiplication,
    //     and its sign handling depends on the denominator's sign. Not mechanical.
    //   - Proportion / Percent / Probability / Cardinal / SafetyFactor — trivially
    //     order on their single numeric field, but they are not IIndex implementors
    //     and their bodies belong to numbers.types.plato / engineering-*.plato territory.
    //   - Instant / BeatTime (time) — single-field, order on SecondsSinceEpoch
    //     and Beats respectively; concrete bodies for the time domain.
    //   - FrameTime (time) — carries Frame AND Rate. Comparing on Frame alone is
    //     WRONG whenever two FrameTimes carry different rates; a correct body
    //     must convert both to seconds. Explicitly not mechanical.
    //   - Boolean / String / Character (primitives) — host-intrinsic orders
    //     (false < true, lexicographic, code-point). Not expressible on an interface.
    // TODO(cross-package): fill the above in their owning packages.

    //==
    // IEquatable
    //
    // Inequality is the negation of equality, once, for every IEquatable. Written
    // against `Equals` explicitly rather than the `!=` operator, which desugars
    // to this very function. Added by plato-378 so that Number, Integer and
    // Boolean no longer each need a NotEquals intrinsic.

    // True when the two values are not equal.
    NotEquals(a: IEquatable, b: IEquatable): Boolean
        => !a.Equals(b);
```
